notes.claim: An eigenvector is a direction a transformation only stretches or squishes, and its eigenvalue is the factor by which it is stretched.
Non-trivial eigenvectors exist exactly when det(A − λI) = 0.
The eigenvalues of a square matrix add up to the sum of its diagonal entries, the trace, which gives a check on the answer.
For i5: two masses coupled by springs have the eigenvectors (1, 1) and (−1, 1), each with its own eigenvalue; these are the system's simple ways to move, its normal modes.
